description: Everyday friction in buying things online and in stores: returns and refunds, package deliveries, price tracking and fake deals, warranties and receipts, customer service, subscriptions, and shopping scams.

items.title: Forgotten return deadlines
items.problem: Items bought online sit in the closet until the return window quietly closes, so people end up keeping things they never wanted.
items.who: frequent online shoppers, especially clothing buyers
items.workaround: calendar reminders, leaving the box by the door, or just eating the cost
items.source_quote: Stop losing money on forgotten returns

items.title: Not knowing when refund lands
items.problem: After mailing a return, the shopper has no idea whether the retailer received it or when the money will actually hit their card, so they keep checking statements.
items.workaround: manually checking bank statements and retailer order pages
items.source_quote: alerts users the moment their refund hits their credit card

items.title: Returns scattered across retailers
items.problem: Each retailer has its own return process, portal, label and deadline, so managing several open returns at once means juggling many emails and accounts.
items.workaround: searching email for order confirmations one by one
items.source_quote: managing and returning online orders from all retailers in one simple app

items.title: Per-item return policy exceptions
items.problem: A receipt with ten items can have different return windows and rules per item (final sale, electronics 15 days, etc.), and nobody reads the fine print until it is too late.
items.who: people who buy many categories at once
items.workaround: assume everything is 30 days and hope
items.source_quote: matches it to the store's policy and subcategory exceptions

items.title: Fake pre-sale price hikes
items.problem: Retailers raise the price days before a sale event and then 'discount' it back to the normal price, so shoppers cannot tell if a sale is real.
items.who: deal hunters during Prime Day, Black Friday and similar events
items.workaround: checking CamelCamelCamel or Keepa price history manually
items.source_quote: bumped up to $119 right before Black Friday, then dropped back to $89 with a 26% off tag

items.title: Permanent 'discounts' that mean nothing
items.problem: Many products are 'on sale' more than half the time, so the strikethrough price is fiction and shoppers cannot judge what a fair price really is.
items.workaround: ignoring list prices; asking friends what they paid
items.source_quote: most discounts being available more than half the time

items.title: Price history only exists for Amazon
items.problem: Price history tools cover Amazon well but not most other retailers, so buyers of furniture, appliances or clothing elsewhere still shop blind.
items.workaround: screenshotting prices and checking back later
items.source_quote: CamelCamelCamel browser extension tells you the pricing history of any Amazon item

items.title: Price drops right after purchase
items.problem: The thing you bought last week goes on sale, and you do not know whether the store offers a price adjustment or how to claim it before the adjustment window ends.
items.workaround: noticing by chance and calling support, or rebuying and returning

items.title: Comparing true total cost across stores
items.problem: The cheapest listed price often loses once shipping, tax, membership fees and return shipping are added, and comparing that total across several sites is manual work.
items.workaround: opening several tabs and adding items to carts to see final totals

items.title: Waiting for a restock or price target
items.problem: A wanted item is out of stock or above budget, and the shopper has to remember to keep checking back across multiple stores.
items.workaround: retailer-specific stock alerts, bookmarks, periodic manual checks

items.title: Coupon codes that never work
items.problem: Shoppers try a string of expired or ineligible coupon codes at checkout and waste time before giving up or paying full price.
items.workaround: browser coupon extensions with hit-or-miss results

items.title: Shrinkflation and unit-price confusion
items.problem: Package sizes shrink while prices stay flat, and comparing per-unit prices across brands and pack sizes in the aisle or online is tedious.
items.workaround: reading tiny shelf unit-price labels or mental math

items.title: Warranty expiry dates unknown
items.problem: By the time an appliance or gadget breaks, nobody remembers when it was bought or whether it is still under warranty, so claims are missed.
items.workaround: digging through email or a drawer of receipts
items.source_quote: push notification 30 days before a warranty is about to expire

items.title: Receipts and manuals lost
items.problem: Paper receipts fade or get tossed, and product manuals vanish, so when something needs a return, warranty claim or repair the proof and instructions are gone.
items.workaround: shoebox of receipts, photographing them, searching email
items.source_quote: keep track of purchase dates, expiration timelines, and serial numbers in one place

items.title: Serial numbers and proof of purchase
items.problem: Warranty claims and insurance reports demand serial numbers, model numbers and purchase proof that are printed on the item or long-gone packaging.
items.who: people filing warranty or theft/insurance claims
items.workaround: photographing labels after the fact, if the item is still around
items.source_quote: add adjacent essentials like invoices or product receipts as well as user manuals

items.title: Extended warranty worth-it decision
items.problem: At checkout the shopper must decide in seconds whether an extended warranty or protection plan is worth it, with no data on failure rates or what the card already covers.
items.workaround: guessing, or defaulting to 'no'

items.title: Product recalls go unnoticed
items.problem: Recalls for items already in the home (cribs, heaters, food) are announced but owners rarely hear about them because nobody connects purchases to recall notices.
items.workaround: none, or luck via news

items.title: Chatbots that do not understand
items.problem: Support chatbots misread the issue and loop through canned answers, forcing customers to rephrase repeatedly before getting anywhere.
items.workaround: typing 'agent' repeatedly, calling instead
items.source_quote: top customer service pain point was 'talking to a bot that doesn't understand me'

items.title: Dreading long hold times
items.problem: People put off resolving billing errors or broken products because they expect to sit on hold for an hour, so problems linger unresolved.
items.workaround: calling at odd hours, speakerphone while working
items.source_quote: Two-thirds of respondents say they hesitate to contact customer service because they expect long hold times

items.title: Repeating the story to every agent
items.problem: Each transfer or follow-up call starts from zero: order number, what happened, what was promised last time, because there is no shared record the customer controls.
items.workaround: keeping notes in a text file, asking for case numbers
items.source_quote: 65% of consumers say that contacting customer service multiple times to resolve a single issue is a key pain point

items.title: Getting a human on the line
items.problem: Escalating from an automated system to a real person is deliberately hard, with hidden menu options and no obvious path.
items.workaround: pressing 0 repeatedly, GetHuman-style cheat sheets
items.source_quote: 56% say it's difficult to escalate to a live agent when needed

items.title: Slow, vague email support replies
items.problem: Support emails take days to answer and the answers are often unclear or do not address the question, stretching a simple issue over weeks.
items.workaround: chasing with follow-up emails, posting on social media
items.source_quote: 51% of customers say that it takes too long to get a response from support agents via email

items.title: Tracking an open complaint's promises
items.problem: Agents promise callbacks, refunds 'in 5-7 days' or replacement shipments, and the customer has no easy way to track what was promised, by whom, and when to chase.
items.workaround: notes app, screenshots of chat transcripts

items.title: Chargeback and dispute timelines
items.problem: When a refund never arrives, filing a card dispute involves unclear deadlines, evidence requirements and weeks of silence.
items.workaround: calling the bank and waiting

items.title: Subscriptions designed to be uncancellable
items.problem: Cancelling a subscription means hunting hidden buttons, sitting through retention pitches or being told to phone during business hours.
items.workaround: cancelling the card, emailing repeatedly
items.source_quote: One frustrated Reddit user recently shared that canceling a subscription seemed impossible

items.title: Locked out of the account to cancel
items.problem: A subscription tied to an old email or lost login keeps charging because the company will not cancel without access to that account.
items.who: people who changed jobs or emails
items.workaround: bank-level block on the merchant
items.source_quote: With that email no longer accessible, the service said it was unable to process a cancellation

items.title: Forgotten recurring charges
items.problem: Free trials convert and small monthly charges pile up unnoticed across cards, and the person cannot list what they are actually paying for.
items.workaround: reviewing statements line by line once a year
items.source_quote: FTC received about 70 consumer complaints a day in 2024 about recurring subscriptions

items.title: Unused gift cards and store credit
items.problem: Gift cards, store credits and refund vouchers get forgotten in drawers or email, and their balances are lost or expire.
items.workaround: a pile of cards in a wallet, checking balances by phone

items.title: Loyalty points expiring unnoticed
items.problem: Points and rewards across dozens of retailer programs expire or sit unredeemed because there is no single view of balances and deadlines.
items.who: shoppers enrolled in multiple loyalty programs
items.workaround: logging into each program occasionally

items.title: Tracking updates lag hours behind
items.problem: Aggregator apps show stale status, so people still have to open each carrier's site to learn where a package really is.
items.workaround: visiting the carrier site directly
items.source_quote: having to visit the actual carrier tracking website to find out where their package is

items.title: Manually entering tracking numbers
items.problem: Order confirmation emails contain the tracking info, yet apps fail to pull it automatically and the user must copy numbers by hand for every order.
items.workaround: copy-paste from email, or relying on each store's own app
items.source_quote: can't figure out how to pull tracking information from order confirmation emails

items.title: No single view of what arrives when
items.problem: With several packages in flight, there is no clear list ordered by expected arrival, so people cannot plan who needs to be home.
items.workaround: scrolling through many emails and apps
items.source_quote: aren't displayed in chronological order, making it annoying to scan the entire list

items.title: Notification spam for old packages
items.problem: Tracking apps keep pinging about packages delivered months ago or ones the user never tracked, burying the alerts that matter.
items.workaround: muting notifications entirely
items.source_quote: constantly send notifications about packages that were delivered months ago

items.title: Failed delivery without a knock
items.problem: The driver never rings or even approaches the door, yet the tracking says 'attempted delivery' and the recipient has to chase a redelivery or pick up at a depot.
items.who: apartment dwellers and people working from home
items.workaround: watching for the truck, doorbell cameras, complaining to the carrier
items.source_quote: watching the truck stop and leave in under 5 seconds without the driver even walking to the door

items.title: Waiting home all day for a delivery
items.problem: Signature-required or large-item deliveries come with a vague all-day window, so people burn a day off waiting and still sometimes get nothing.
items.who: people receiving furniture, appliances or signature packages
items.workaround: refreshing tracking, calling the carrier for an ETA
items.source_quote: A day wasted waiting on FedEx AGAIN

items.title: Packages stolen from the porch
items.problem: Deliveries left unattended get taken, and the recipient must prove theft to the retailer or carrier to get a replacement.
items.workaround: shipping to work, lockers, doorbell cameras
items.source_quote: Taking possession of a package or its contents, outside of a residence or business

items.title: Marked delivered but not received
items.problem: Tracking says delivered, nothing is at the door, and the shopper must figure out whether it went to a neighbor, the wrong address, or was stolen, then convince support.
items.workaround: checking with neighbors, waiting 48 hours, filing claims

items.title: Coordinating deliveries with household
items.problem: Roommates or family members do not know whose package arrived, who signed for it, or where it was put, leading to lost and mistakenly opened parcels.
items.workaround: group chats and sticky notes

items.title: Missing items in a delivered order
items.problem: Multi-item orders ship in parts, and the shopper cannot tell whether a missing item is still coming or was left out of the box until they audit every shipment.
items.workaround: rereading shipping emails and comparing to the box contents

items.title: Grocery delivery substitutions
items.problem: Delivered groceries include unwanted substitutions or missing staples, discovered only when unpacking, and reporting each item for credit is tedious.
items.workaround: checking the app during shopping, filing refunds afterwards

items.title: Is this online store legit?
items.problem: A store with a great price and a plausible site may be a scam, and checking domain age, reviews and contact details takes research most shoppers skip.
items.who: anyone buying from an unfamiliar site
items.workaround: searching '<store> scam' on Reddit, Trustpilot lookups
items.source_quote: search Reddit for '[store name] review' or '[store name] scam'

items.title: Social media ad scam stores
items.problem: Instagram and Facebook ads push heavily discounted products from cookie-cutter template shops that ship nothing or junk, and shoppers cannot tell them from real brands.
items.workaround: only buying from known brands
items.source_quote: advertise heavily discounted products via Facebook/Instagram ads, provide fake tracking numbers or ship worthless items

items.title: Fake tracking numbers from sellers
items.problem: Scam or sloppy sellers supply tracking numbers that never move or belong to someone else's shipment, leaving the buyer unsure whether to wait or dispute.
items.workaround: waiting past the estimate and then opening a dispute
items.source_quote: provide fake tracking numbers

items.title: Trusting product reviews
items.problem: Shoppers rely on star ratings but know many reviews are bought or merged from unrelated products, and fake-review checkers only guess.
items.workaround: Fakespot/ReviewMeta, reading only 1-star and 3-star reviews
items.source_quote: these are just algorithms that don't actually know which reviews are fake

items.title: Counterfeits from marketplace sellers
items.problem: Commingled inventory and third-party sellers mean a branded product may arrive counterfeit or 'not as described', and proving it for a refund is a hassle.
items.workaround: buying only 'sold by' the brand, checking seller ratings
items.source_quote: Anyone else quickly losing confidence in Amazon?

items.title: Review-request overload
items.problem: Every purchase triggers a stream of emails and app prompts begging for reviews, which clutters the inbox and trains people to ignore all post-purchase mail, including the important ones.
items.workaround: unsubscribing, filters
items.source_quote: increasingly an obligatory burden for shoppers and sellers alike

items.title: Phishing 'delivery problem' texts
items.problem: Fake USPS/FedEx texts about a held package look just like real notifications, and people expecting a parcel cannot tell which alerts are genuine.
items.workaround: never clicking links, checking the carrier site manually

items.title: Guessing clothing sizes online
items.problem: Brand sizing is inconsistent and shoppers do not know their own measurements, so they buy two or three sizes and return the rest.
items.workaround: bracketing sizes and returning, reading fit comments
items.source_quote: 40% of online returns are a result of an incorrect size selection

items.title: Inconsistent sizing between brands
items.problem: A medium in one brand is a large in another, and nothing remembers which size fit last time from each store.
items.workaround: notes app with sizes per brand, or memory
items.source_quote: many brands are not consistent with sizing

items.title: Forced app downloads and accounts
items.problem: Retailers push shoppers to install yet another app or create an account to check out or get the deal, and people resent the clutter and data exposure.
items.workaround: guest checkout, deleting the app afterwards
items.source_quote: Thirty-seven percent of respondents said they did not want to download retail apps because they already have too many

items.title: Wishlists scattered across stores
items.problem: Items saved for later live in a dozen retailer accounts and browser tabs, so people forget what they wanted or buy duplicates.
items.workaround: bookmarks, screenshots, notes app

items.title: Rebuying what you already own
items.problem: People buy a second charger, spice or tool because they forgot they already had one at home.
items.workaround: texting a family member to check, or none

items.title: Promotional email flood
items.problem: Every purchase adds another daily marketing newsletter, and the real order updates get lost among sales blasts.
items.workaround: unsubscribing one at a time, throwaway email addresses
